chapter_title: The Involvement of Purinergic System in Pain: Adenosine Receptors and Inosine as Pharmacological Tools in Future Treatments
source_pdf: /mnt/project-files/Experimental Provenance for QSAR Dataset/Pharmacology (Luca Gallelli) (z-library.sk, 1lib.sk, z-lib.sk).pdf

records.mechanism_book_wording: activation of P1 receptors by adenosine decreases pain, inflammation, and cellular excitability
records.quote: activation of P1 receptors by adenosine decreases pain, inflammation, and cellular excitability
records.notes: Page 641 calls adenosine 'the natural ligand of P1 receptors, also called adenosine receptors'.

records.mechanism_book_wording: due to its activation of A1R
records.quote: due to its activation of A1R, and as a diagnostic for myocardial perfusion imaging
records.notes: Adenosine is described as the only adenosine agonist used in humans for a long time; used for paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (Adenocard).

records.mechanism_book_wording: utilizing its A2AR-activating effects resulting in vasodilation
records.quote: utilizing its A2AR-activating effects resulting in vasodilation
records.notes: Diagnostic use for myocardial perfusion imaging (Adenoscan).

others is an antagonist of adenosine receptors.

records.role_detail: activator (direct or indirect); agonist/partial agonist status left open by the book
records.mechanism_book_wording: Inosine in a direct or indirect way activates A1R to induce analgesia
records.quote: Inosine in a direct or indirect way activates A1R to induce analgesia
records.notes: Section 4.5.1 (PDF 650) says it is not possible to affirm whether inosine is a natural ligand or a partial agonist of adenosine receptors. Page 648 says anti-inflammatory effects seem mediated by A1R, A2R and A3R. Role Agonist is the nearer rule name.

records.role_detail: activator; agonist/partial agonist status left open by the book
records.mechanism_book_wording: Inosine activates A2AR to induce analgesia
records.quote: Inosine activates A2AR to induce analgesia, at least in the acetic acid
records.notes: Quote continues on PDF 650 ('model'). Book says A2AR role in inosine analgesia in other pain models might be different or not exist.

records.mechanism_book_wording: inosine binds to A3R in mast cells
records.quote: demonstrated that inosine binds to A3R in mast cells, but not to A1R or A2AR
records.notes: Book says binding only; role Agonist is inferred for the rule name. Same page: Fredholm group observed inosine weakly bound to A1 and A3 but not A2; book says A2BR and A3R are not involved in inosine analgesic effect.

records.mechanism_book_wording: a natural activator of adenosine receptors
records.quote: Inosine might be a natural activator of adenosine receptors.
records.notes: Stated as a possibility ('might be').

records.role_detail: inhibition of PKC pathway (indirect, mechanism unclear)
records.mechanism_book_wording: the analgesic action of inosine depends on PKC inhibition
records.quote: the analgesic action of inosine depends on PKC inhibition
records.notes: Book says it is not clear how this happens; inosine inhibits pain caused by a PKC activator.

records.quote: AK inhibitors are able to decrease pain levels when given peripherally or sistemically
records.quote_corrected_reading: AK inhibitors are able to decrease pain levels when given peripherally or systemically
records.notes: Class named without a compound in this chapter's body text.

records.quote: inhibitors of ADA itself are able to cause analgesia in determined animal models
records.notes: Page 647 section 3.8.3 also states 'inhibition of adenosine deaminase prolonged the analgesic effect of acupuncture in mice'.

records.role_detail: enzyme supplied exogenously to raise adenosine; not an activator of the enzyme
records.mechanism_book_wording: exogenous supply of NT5E (increases supply of adenosine)
records.quote: exogenous supply of NT5E (increases supply of adenosine)
records.notes: Weak fit: the enzyme itself is the agent, not a ligand of it. Role Activator is a forced choice of the nearer rule name; flagged for later filtering.

records.notes: The sentence does not state target or role; both are inferred from its position after the A3R agonist sentences. Treat as uncertain.

records.quote: SDZ WAG 994 (adenosine A1R agonist)
records.numbers_detail: single dose 0.1 - 0.5 mg/kg in a phase I trial; 1 mg/kg in a double-blind trial (PDF 652)
records.notes: 1 mg/kg did not differ from placebo for postoperative dental pain; higher doses gave dose-dependent adverse events.

records.quote: Another full high-affinity A1R agonists, GR79236X, was also evaluated
records.numbers_detail: 15-min double-blind infusion containing 10 ug/kg (PDF 652; printed as micro-g/kg)
records.notes: No evidence of efficacy versus placebo in dental pain, per the book.

records.quote: Another A1R agonist GW493838 developed by GlaxoSmithKline
records.notes: Phase II trials; further development discontinued per the book.

records.quote: selective allosteric enhancer T-62, given orally
records.notes: Allosteric enhancer is mapped to Agonist as the nearer role; the book does not say agonist. Phase I trials completed for neuropathic pain.

records.quote: the A2AR agonist BVT.115959 from Biovitrum
records.notes: Completed clinical trials for diabetic neuropathic pain; well tolerated but no significant improvement of pain symptoms.

records.quote: intrathecal injection of A1R agonists cause analgesia
records.notes: Class statement without a named compound.

records.quote: only one spinal injection of A2AR agonist was able to induce analgesia
records.notes: Class statement without a named compound. Page 645 notes A2AR activation is reported to induce pain in some studies and reduce it in others.
